full_judgment: 12. With regard to allegation against the ACNABIN, Mr lmran Anwar contends that there is an allegation against a partner of ACNABIN named Mr Rokunuzzaman, FCA in relation to their work for Aman Feed Limited, which has nothing to do with the present case, because the partner involved in this case is Mr Mominul Karim FCA. He contends that the allegation raised by the BSEC on this score is contrary to established legal maxim of "presumption of innocence until proven guilty" and, more importantly, ACNABIN is listed as a recognized accounting firm both by the BSEC and Bangladesh Bank, and just because there is allegation against one of their partners does not invalidate their work or their credibility, particularly when a different partner, as in this present case, carries out the work. Mr lmran Anwar, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, argues that there have been numerous communications between the petitioner companies and the BSEC regarding this merger and, in none of these occasions, the BSEC raised any issue of objection relating to the amalgamation, nor did it issue any letter of objection to the transferee company or the transferor company. He contends that ACNABIN being not disqualified from carrying out the audit work or valuation work by any Court in Bangladesh or by any regulatory authority and, in the absence of such disqualification, ACNABIN's report should not be questioned inasmuch as that would render all work of ACNABIN invalid, questionable and dubious since the point of time when the allegation was raised; that the petitioners engaged ACNABIN because it is a widely reputed chartered accountant firm who has considerable experience in carrying out audit and valuation work; that the valuation was carried out much earlier compared to the point in time when the allegation against ACNABIN was raised and the allegation relating to Aman Feed has no connection with regard to the valuation in the present case so as to render their entire work unreliable. Mr Imran Anwar submits that there is no illegality in the valuation process, as not a single one that the respondent BSEC has been able to point out, nor has there been any violation or non-compliance of legal provision in carrying out the valuation exercise and so there is no justification to appoint an audit firm adding costs and complexity to the process of amalgamation. He submits that there is no requirement under law for appointment of valuation expert in the given scenario where a valuation has already been conducted by an independent audit firm having enlistment with the BSEC and the Bangladesh Bank. He claims that this petition is completely a bona fide one.
